title: scHGNN: A single-cell gene regulatory network inference method based on heuristic graph neural networks
abstract: The construction of gene regulatory networks based on single-cell transcriptomics (scRNA-seq) data provides crucial technical support for decoding cell fate determination mechanisms at the single-cell level, elucidating molecular mechanisms underlying disease progression, and developing targeted therapeutics. Existing methods for constructing GRNs often rely excessively on gene expression features, struggling to achieve an effective balance between local direct regulatory signals and global multi-step regulatory pathways.

title: Low-Temperature Aqueous Upgrading of Waste PET Plastics into Metal–Organic Frameworks with Confined PdNi Clusters for High-Performance Semihydrogenation of Alkynes
abstract: The selective semihydrogenation of alkynes to alkenes is an important industrial process for the production of bulk and fine chemicals. However, the activity and selectivity trade-off of alkyne hydrogenation has been a long-standing challenge, due to undesirable overhydrogenation or insufficient activity of the designed catalysts. Here, we report a sustainable route for high-performance alkyne hydrogenation using a metal–organic framework (MOF) confined PdNi cluster (PdcNi) catalyst, synthesized directly from waste polyethylene terephthalate (PET) plastics under low-temperature aqueous…
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Oriented Charge Flow in a Dual-Active-Site CdS Framework Enables Coupled CO2 Reduction and Biomass Alcohol Oxidation
abstract: Solar-driven conversion of CO2 into value-added chemicals provides an effective pathway for carbon resource utilization. However, the sluggish kinetics of CO2 reduction and the reliance on sacrificial electron donors limit its practical viability. Herein, we present a bifunctional photocatalyst consisting of spatially separated Ag2S and Au cocatalysts anchored on hollow CdS (Ag2S-Au/CdSH), which enables efficient concurrent CO2 photoreduction to CO and selective oxidation of aryl alcohols to benzaldehyde in a sacrificial-agent-free system.

title: HyScale: Scaling Long-Context Training for Learned Sparse Attention
abstract: We present HyScale, a long-context training system for learned sparse attention. Learned sparse attention is a promising architecture for million-token contexts, widely adopted in production since DeepSeek-V3.2. Selection, however, grows into the training bottleneck. For each query, it scores every previous token whereas sparse attention reads only $k$; worse, current systems materialize a full score table and repeat selection during recomputation. Our key insight is that the output of selection is not an activation, but rather a set of indices. Building on it, HyScale introduces HyTopK and selection replay. HyTopK finds each query's exact top-$k$ on the fly without a score table, while selection replay reuses forward-pass selection in recomputation. Together with holistic system optimizations tackling end-to-end training challenges, HyScale speeds up GLM-5.1 training on 1M-token sequences by 2.07$\times$ over Megatron-LM on 512 H20 GPUs. It also speeds up the CSA layers of DeepSeek-V4-Flash and the QSA layers of Qwen3.8-Flash-Next by 2.01$\times$ and 1.57$\times$ at 1M tokens on 32 H800 GPUs.

title: NUViT: Vision Transformers for Fourier Space Data
abstract: Vision Transformers (ViTs) have demonstrated strong performance in many computer vision tasks but do not naturally extend beyond the natural image domain. One important example is Fourier-space data, which is used to represent a rich and diverse set of modalities, including medical imaging and microscopy. Standard ViT tokenization partitions an image into square patches on a Cartesian grid, which poorly fit the frequency and phase structure of Fourier-space data. We introduce Non-Uniform ViT, a simple, general-purpose vision transformer that redesigns image tokenization, data representation, and positional encoding to respect this structure. Experiments on Fourier-domain image classification, 2D crystal lattice identification, MRI annotation, and cryo-EM protein heterogeneity analysis show that NUViT consistently captures the structure of Fourier data better than standard architectures.

title: Do AI-for-Science Agents Preserve Model Safety?
abstract: AI-for-Science agents are increasingly being used for formulating scientific hypotheses, running autonomous experiments, and interpreting evidence. These agents are constructed by integrating a large language model (LLM) into a domain-specific agent harness, which in turn can improve the LLM's scientific capability and enable the model to orchestrate scientific tools. In this work, we ask whether model safety is preserved when an LLM is integrated in an AI-for-Science agent harness. We evaluate five agent harnesses on 50 harmful chemistry requests. Specifically, we study how the safety behavior changes under direct prompting, two simple adversarial prompting strategies, and an adaptive attack. Across four recent GPT variants, our results show that the agent harness can increase harmful compliance even under direct prompting. More critically, we find that adaptive attacks that are largely unsuccessful against the base LLM suddenly become highly successful after the agent harness is introduced. Our results show that the safety behavior of the base LLM is not durable once a harness is introduced. Thus, as AI-for-Science agents become more capable and autonomous, the community needs to evaluate and align the agent using domain-specific safety benchmarks.

title: RADIANT: Object-Centric Feed-Forward Global Illumination
abstract: Feed-forward neural renderers synthesize global illumination across novel 3D scenes without per-scene optimization or runtime ray tracing. Existing transformer-based renderers tokenize individual triangles, so self-attention scales quadratically with mesh resolution. Yet macroscopic radiative transport is governed by the underlying surface geometry and object arrangements rather than a particular mesh discretization; finer tessellation can thus inflate token counts without changing the underlying transport physics, motivating a discretization-agnostic and object-centric representation. We introduce RADIANT (RADiance-based Inter-Actor Neural Transformer), an object-centric architecture for feed-forward global illumination from point inputs. By representing each object with a compact budget of 32 surface-patch tokens, RADIANT decouples attention sequence length from polygon counts. In a single network, an inter-object scene transformer models 3D radiative exchange and a view decoder renders images at target camera poses. To capture light transport without materializing O(N^2) bias matrices, invariant form-factor attention embeds geometric distances and surface orientations directly into query-key dot products as SE(3)-invariant inner products weighted by learned area and material gains. For primary visibility without mesh connectivity, camera rays cross-attend scene tokens guided by depth-tested point splats in a shared spherical frame. Across a 1.03M-scene benchmark under matched model capacity, RADIANT reaches 25 dB tone-mapped PSNR in 5x fewer training steps than RenderFormer, and achieves 32.2 dB at 600k steps (+3.3 dB over RenderFormer and +7.6 dB over RenderFormer-V2). We further demonstrate the scalability of RADIANT, which completes a 512x512 forward pass of a 500-object scene in 0.83 s, with computational cost scaling with the number of objects rather than polygons.

title: Boundary shape controls the stress distribution in two-component elastic materials
abstract: We investigate how the shape and arrangement of high-stiffness regions govern stress redistribution in two-component triangular elastic spring networks subjected to spatially correlated and uncorrelated random prestress. We compare boundary roughness, partitioning into disconnected regions, and graded transitions between regions of different stiffness. Our simulations identify interface bonds as channels for energy transfer: increasing their number provides additional transfer paths and reduces stress concentration in mechanically rigid regimes, while offering little benefit in compliant subnetworks. This is analogous to defects in naturally occurring crystal structures, where the defects themselves isolate stress. At a fixed fraction of high-stiffness material, partitioning reduces stress concentration for both correlated and uncorrelated prestress. The benefit diminishes with further subdivision as the number of interface bonds becomes comparable to the number of interior nodes. Stress reduction, however, depends on the spatial correlations of the imposed prestress: random prestress generally yields a stronger effect, though the difference diminishes in some regimes. Graded interfaces further reduce peak stress by distributing the stiffness transition over a broader region. Together, these results suggest design strategies based on increasing interface area, matching subdivision scale to prestress correlations, and grading stiffness transitions. This minimal framework identifies how internal structure controls energy transfer and stress redistribution, suggesting design principles for mechanical robustness under both internal and external loading.

title: Cross-coupled photon avalanche drives room-temperature intrinsic optical bistability
abstract: Optically bistable materials promise technological advances in optical information processing, memristive devices, and multiparametric sensing. However, optical bistability is predominantly observed under cryogenic conditions or is governed by subtle thermo-optical nonlinearities. Here, we report on Ho3+-activated nanocrystals that exhibit cavity-free intrinsic optical bistability (IOB) at ambient conditions. Non-thermal IOB stems from a cross-coupled photon avalanche (XPA) mechanism enabled by a low-phonon-energy double-perovskite host, which reduces nonradiative losses and facilitates excited-state population via XPA, even when the pump intensity is below threshold. Time-resolved luminescence measurements support the proposed XPA, as evidenced by a double-rise profile consistent with two reservoir states interlocked in energy looping. IOB with high-contrast photoswitching (up to 46 dB) is observed at room temperature across multiple visible emission lines, enabling wavelength-division multiplexing and compatibility with common detectors. IOB is preserved across nano- to microscale crystals and different double-perovskite compositions, broadly enabling information photonics and advanced sensing.

title: Zero photoemission from icosahedral superatoms
abstract: Photoemission is expected to occur when the photon energy exceeds the binding energy of an electron, with the photoemission yield generally remaining non-zero above this threshold. Yet, it can be suppressed at specific photon energies, a phenomenon known as the Cooper minimum. Although complete suppression represents an extreme limit of this phenomenon, such zero photoemission has previously been reported only for atoms with an outermost s-type orbital and has never been observed in non-atomic systems. Here, we demonstrate the deliberate realization of zero photoemission from Ag12W-, an artificial icosahedral superatom, by observing a vanishing photoemission cross section 0.85 eV above the detachment threshold and reproducing this behavior in theoretical simulations. These simulations predict that zero photoemission can be common in nearly spherical nanoclusters, a prediction we experimentally confirm using Ag12Mo-, an isoelectronic counterpart of Ag12W-. Because superatoms offer systematic control over both size and elemental composition using the periodic table, our findings establish a route toward active control of photoemission in finite-size quantum systems and stimulate further investigations of underexplored physical phenomena such as nondipole effects.

title: Heterogeneous superconductivity emerging from a charge-stripe state in kagome lattices
abstract: Charge density wave (CDW) and superconductivity have long been recognized as competing orders. However, recent achievements establish that the interplay between these two collective electronic phenomena can be more perplexing, with emergent phenomena arising from their cooperation. Here we report a distinctive case of the kagome superconductors CsV3Sb5-xSnx, in which the characteristics of superconductivity evolve in accordance with the form of CDW order. As the triple-Q CDW in CsV3Sb5 transforms to a short-range stripelike CDW at xc = 0.07, a sudden change in superconducting properties occurs concomitantly. A combination of thermodynamic, electrical transport and scanning tunneling microscopy experiments reveals a heterogeneous superconducting state beyond xc: the superconducting gap exhibits pronounced spatial variation, in conformity with a distribution of critical temperature and the resulted superconducting precursor effects. Moreover, abundant normal fluid persists deep into the superconducting state, as evidenced by remnants of electronic specific heat and zero-energy quasiparticle interference. These observations are unrelated to the chemical inhomogeneity and residual strain effect introduced by Sn substitution. Instead, they emulate the phenomenology that a sign-changing superconducting order parameter is subject to strong pair-breaking scattering with the short-range charge stripes and hence reflect the unconventional nature of superconductivity developing inside the charge-stripe state.

title: DIELECTRIC CONTINUUM MODELING FOR THE DE NOVO DESIGNED CALCIUM CHANNEL CALC6.3: STRUCTURE PREPARATION, MESHGENERATION, AND CALCIUM SELECTIVITY
abstract: This paper presents an integrated software package for continuum dielectric studies of the de novo designed calcium channel CalC6.3. The package combines Python scripts for cleaning and repairing the original PDB structure (PDB ID: 9DZW) with PDB2PQR to generate a corre-sponding PQR file containing atomic coordinates, partial charges, and radii. It incorporates the Gaussian Ion Channel Molecular Surface Generation package to construct high-quality triangular molecular surface meshes that preserve the complex channel pore geometry while maintaining suffi-nterface-fitted tetrahedral meshes of a simulation box consisting of protein, membrane, and solvent regions. The integrated software package further integrates the structure-preparation and mesh- size-nite element solver to compute electrostatic potentials and ionic concentrations, streamlining the complete workflow from structure preparation to numerical solution. Numerical experiments for an ionic solution containing Ca2+, Na+ , and Cl-ions show preferential Ca2+ accumulation in the narrow selectivity filter formed by six Glu residues, supporting the experimentally observed calcium selectivity of CalC6.3. They also suggest that a smoother molecular surface mesh can improve the convergence and performance of the finite element solver.

title: Mixed Quantum/Classical Theory for Fine-Structure Inelastic Transitions in the Scattering of 2Π Molecule with Structureless Target
abstract: Mixed Quantum/Classical Theory (MQCT) offers an efficient alternative for computing molecular scattering cross sections, scaling favorably with the size of the basis as compared to the exact close-coupling methods. In this work, the MQCT framework is extended to the rotationally inelastic scattering of 2Π molecules with structureless targets, using the Ar + NO (X2Π) system as a benchmark. The time-dependent equations of motion are solved for independent MQCT trajectories by treating the translational motion classically and the electronic and rotational motions quantum mechanically.
venue: Journal of Chemical Theory and Computation

title: Promoting Efficient H2 Dissociation in Photothermal CO2 Hydrogenation through Functional Separation and Synergistic Coupling of Active Sites
abstract: Efficient H2 dissociation and subsequent spillover of active hydrogen species are critical factors for achieving high activity in CO2 hydrogenation reactions. Herein, we constructed a well-designed and highly dispersed Cu–In bimetallic catalyst supported on CeO2. This catalyst enables the spatial separation of plasmonic enhancement, H2 activation, and CO2 conversion sites, thereby significantly improving H2 dissociation capability and H-spillover efficiency.

title: Artificial intelligence in hepatitis: Advances in diagnosis, treatment optimization, and prognostic prediction
abstract: Hepatitis remains a major global health challenge and an important contributor to liver fibrosis, cirrhosis, hepatocellular carcinoma, and liver-related mortality worldwide. Early diagnosis, effective treatment selection, and accurate prognostic stratification remain critical unmet needs in clinical hepatology. Artificial intelligence, particularly machine learning and deep learning, has emerged as a promising approach to addressing these challenges through the integration and analysis of large-scale, heterogeneous biomedical datasets. This narrative review synthesizes advances in artificial intelligence applications in hepatitis research and clinical practice published over the past decade, organized across three clinical domains: diagnosis, treatment optimization, and prognosis prediction. In the diagnostic domain, artificial intelligence-based approaches have been applied to medical imaging, digital pathology, and multi-omics data to enhance the detection, classification, and staging of liver disease. In the therapeutic domain, machine learning models have been increasingly deployed to support drug discovery, optimize therapeutic regimens, and predict individual treatment responses. In the prognostic domain, artificial intelligence-driven models have shown promising performance in predicting disease progression, survival outcomes, and clinical complications. Nevertheless, key limitations persist, including data heterogeneity, limited external generalizability, and barriers to clinical translation. Future progress will depend on prospective multicenter evaluation, use of interoperable multimodal data, development of transparent models that account for uncertainty, and evidence that artificial intelligence improves clinical decisions and patient outcomes rather than performance metrics alone.
venue: The Journal of international medical research

title: Extended Reality, Telementoring, and Artificial Intelligence-Assisted Assessment in Surgical Training: A Narrative Review
abstract: ObjectiveThe Halstedian apprenticeship model in surgical training faces escalating pressure from work-hour restrictions, rising operative complexity, and heightened patient-safety expectations. Extended reality (XR) technologies-virtual reality (VR), augmented reality (AR), and mixed reality (MR)-together with telementoring platforms and artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted assessment, are frequently proposed as responses to these pressures.

title: Computationally Guided Design of Two Novel Phosphodiesterase-4 Inhibitors for Treatment of Plaque Psoriasis
abstract: Plaque psoriasis is a chronic inflammatory skin disease characterized by itchy, scaly skin. Although there is currently no cure for this disease, it can be managed with medication, such as phosphodiesterase-4 (PDE4) inhibitors. Current PDE4 inhibitors are limited and show adverse effects. With the goal to develop better PDE4 inhibitors for the treatment of plaque psoriasis, two novel drug candidates were designed with computational studies, and observed to have better ADMET properties compared to Roflumilast. A homology analysis was performed to determine the best model organism for preclinical studies of the novel candidates.

title: Acute and 90-Day Repeated-Dose Oral Toxicity of Urtica dioica L. Leaf Extract Granules in Rodents
abstract: Urtica dioica L. leaves are traditionally used in Indonesia for gout-related complaints, and granules formulated from their ethanolic leaf extract have shown xanthine oxidase inhibitory and uric acid-lowering activity; the safety of the finished formulation, however, remains uncharacterised. This study evaluated acute and repeated-dose oral toxicity under Indonesian National Agency of Drug and Food Control (BPOM) Regulation No. 10 of 2022. Female Swiss Webster mice received a single dose of 5, 50, 500, or 5000 mg/kg granules, and Sprague-Dawley rats of both sexes (five per sex per group) received 77.5, 155, or 310 mg/kg/day for 13 weeks (90 days), with satellite groups observed through a 30-day recovery period. No mortality occurred at 5000 mg/kg, giving an LD50 above that limit; clinical signs, body weight, and rectal temperature showed no dose-related change. After repeated dosing, erythrocyte indices, blood urea nitrogen, and creatinine were unchanged in both sexes. Leukocyte count rose in high-dose females (p < 0.05) but was not observed in the high-dose recovery group, and liver weight differed among female groups without a dose-response pattern. Weight gain at the highest dose differed from control in both sexes but in opposite directions. Control values outside the strain reference range and baseline body-weight imbalance preclude establishing a no-observed-adverse-effect level.

title: C–C Bond Formation via the Addition or Redistribution of Hydrogen: Chemical Synthesis Beyond Premetalated Reagents or Metallic Reductants
abstract: Stoichiometric organometallic reagents are used in countless C–C bond-forming processes but are often hazardous, display poor functional group compatibility, and require multistep preparation from the parent platform chemicals. Zerovalent metals are also used to mediate reductive C–C bond formation, but their use at scale poses similar safety and engineering concerns.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Designing better adsorbents to remove PFAS from water
abstract: A review by Tohoku University researchers identifies key molecular features that could guide the development of more effective materials for removing PFAS from water. The study is published in the journal ACS Materials Au.

title: Scientists demonstrate AI-designed enzyme for drug synthesis
abstract: The new RFD4-Proteina unified generative model for protein design—created by the Institute for Protein Design (IPD) in collaboration with NVIDIA—uses advanced AI to generate entirely new protein sequences and structures, achieving computational design success rates five to 10 times higher than previous models and generating candidates five to 10 times faster.

title: Advances in Photothermal CO2 Hydrogenation to Methane: Mechanistic Insights into Catalytic System Design across Different Scales
abstract: The ever-escalating accumulation of atmospheric CO2 and the growing demand for renewable energy conversion and storage have intensified research into solar-driven CO2 utilization technologies. Photothermal catalytic CO2 hydrogenation to methane has emerged as a promising approach for simultaneous carbon resource recycling and solar energy conversion, synergistically integrating the merits of photocatalysis and thermocatalysis.

title: UnibindMD: An Integrated AI and Molecular Dynamics Platform for De Novo Peptide Binder Design
abstract: UnibindMD is an integrated computational platform that turns a protein target into validated de novo peptide-binder leads by chaining five orthogonal stages: deep-learning binder design (BindCraft), independent structure prediction and confidence assessment (AlphaFold3-class / Boltz-2), binding-affinity prediction (PRODIGY), developability profiling (ADMET-AI), and all-atom molecular-dynamics validation (GROMACS/CHARMM36m).

title: Biphasic Polyarylisocyanide Liquid Crystals with Enhanced Enantiodiscrimination for Residual Chemical Shift Anisotropy Measurements
abstract: Anisotropic NMR spectroscopy has emerged as a powerful tool for the structural elucidation of complex small molecules. Compared with residual dipolar couplings (RDCs), however, the application of residual chemical shift anisotropies (RCSAs) has remained relatively limited, largely owing to the lack of simple and efficient methods for their acquisition. Here, we report a biphasic polyarylisocyanide lyotropic liquid-crystalline (LLC) system based on single-handed helical polyisocyanides prepared by alkyne-Pd(II)-catalyzed controlled polymerization.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Uncovering Microbial Nitrogenous Chemical Diversity through Isotope-Guided Molecular Networking
abstract: Nitrogen-containing natural products are pivotal sources of bioactive molecules. However, their comprehensive investigation by metabolomics remains challenging due to background interference from primary metabolites and their high structural diversity including peptides, alkaloids, nucleosides, and others. Here, we present NitroVISION, an integrated pipeline that combines stable isotope labeling with targeted molecular networking to selectively detect nitrogen-containing metabolites from a complex mixture.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: SPectroscopy Informed Configurational Enhanced Sampling (SPICES)
abstract: We present a new enhanced-sampling scheme for obtaining the underlying conformer starting from a spectrum: the SPectroscopy Informed Configurational Enhanced Sampling (SPICES) method. SPICES is driven by a history-dependent biased molecular dynamics, in which the biases are governed by spectral information rather than by energetic considerations. The performance of SPICES is hence rather insensitive to the target conformer’s relative energy compared to the global minimum structure. Furthermore, it does not require pretraining or prior knowledge of the system. We have critically assessed the performance of SPICES and demonstrated that it can identify the correct conformer of our test system, diphenylalanine (FF), among the 400 stable conformations in 22 spectral calculations (median value). We also show that SPICES is robust to noise in the experimental spectrum and to small discrepancies between theory and experiment.
venue: Journal of Chemical Theory and Computation

title: Finding the Sweet Spot: Isomerization Strategy Enables Balanced Energy Dissipation of NIR-II AIEgens for “One-for-All” Tumor Phototheranostics
abstract: “One-for-all” phototheranostics with the second near-infrared window (NIR-II) emission have garnered great enthusiasm for seamlessly integrating superb imaging and high-efficiency therapy into a single formula. However, it is still a nontrivial conundrum to achieve balanced excited-state energy dissipation to guarantee high NIR-II brightness, photothermal conversion, and reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Cap-specific N6-adenosine methyltransferases and applications in m6A Cap-1 mRNA synthesis
abstract: In addition to the 5' Cap-1 structure, the initiating adenosine of mammalian mRNA can be further modified by PCIF1 (Phosphorylated C-terminal domain-interacting factor 1) to form 2'-O,N6-dimethyladenosine (m6A Cap-1). While the biological role is still under investigation, the implications of m6A Cap-1 in mRNA metabolism and viral-host interactions have spurred interest in PCIF1 and m6A Cap-1 as biomarkers, drug targets, and research tools. Here, we identify and characterize two PCIF1-like cap-specific N6-adenosine methyltransferases, PC04 and PC05 and evaluate their applicability in m6A Cap-1 mRNA synthesis in vitro. We found that both enzymes are highly specific to the m7G cap structure and highly active on Cap-1 RNA oligonucleotides and trinucleotide Cap-1 analogs at nanomolar concentrations. We demonstrate that PC04 or PC05 methylation reactions can be incorporated into established post-transcriptional capping and cap analog-based co-transcriptional in vitro transcription (IVT) workflows to produce m6A Cap-1 RNAs. Finally, we show that PC05 can be combined with a previously reported FCE::T7 RNA polymerase fusion to synthesize m6A Cap-1 mRNA from DNA templates in a single step, co-transcriptional manner. The robustness of the PCIF1-like cap N6-adenosine methyltransferases can accelerate research into the biological roles of cap m6A modification and development of highly effective mRNA-based therapeutics.

title: In Situ X-ray Spectroscopic Identification and Kinetic Control of Highly Hybridized Co(IV) States in Cobalt Oxide Amorphous Catalysts
abstract: Valence dynamics of transition metals are central to oxygen evolution reaction (OER) mechanisms, yet in situ spectroscopic studies capturing these dynamics within amorphous catalysts remain limited. Here, we present in situ X-ray spectroscopy of amorphous catalysts, where CoBi exhibits higher OER performance compared to CoPi. While our data shows successive valence changes toward high-valent states in both catalysts, distinct initial electro-structural states dictate the intermediate evolution.

title: MycorrhizaFinder: a user-friendly machine-learning tool to quantify endomycorrhizal colonisation of nursery and field roots
abstract: Root colonisation by endomycorrhizal fungi has long been a widely used metric in mycorrhizal studies. However, due to the significant time required to assess colonisation using traditional microscopy techniques, studies of colonisation at large scales are impractical. Machine-learning-based approaches may increase output and facilitate ecosystem assessments. We trained a machine-learning-based tool (MycorrhizaFinder) on 42 field roots (132 unique 1 cm sections, with > 100,000 tiles) and validated on a further 37 sections from grasslands and heathlands hosting common Northern European plants with arbuscular (AM) and ericoid mycorrhizal (ErM) fungal structures, and dark septate endophytes (DSE), also common in field-sourced roots. We incorporated a user-customized confidence threshold to encourage engagement with morphological ambiguities, in e.g. ErM and DSE. A Macro F1 statistic was used to assess the tool's development performance. We provide a sample workflow from root processing and microscope slide scanning to semi-automated model training and performance evaluation. Our model performance combining all classes, the Macro F1, is conservatively 66% for arbuscular and 57% for ericoid mycorrhizal colonisation assessment. MycorrhizaFinder is user-friendly, requires no programming skills and offers flexibility for advanced agronomists or ecologists to train the tool using their own labelled mycorrhizal root datasets, including images acquired from different instruments or staining protocols. This adaptability allows users to customize the model for specific ecosystems or experimental designs. Leveraged with molecular identification and/or functional traits of fungi (e.g. arbuscules), MycorrhizaFinder supports scalable and repeatable nursery experiments and monitoring across ecosystems to assess mycorrhizal status and track land-use changes over time.

title: Vacancy-enhanced Li solid-solution anodes for solid-state batteries: computational screening enabling high critical current density
abstract: Sluggish vacancy-mediated self-diffusion in lithium metal limits the critical current density (CCD) of Li anodes in solid-state batteries by promoting interfacial void formation during stripping. To enhance the effective vacancy concentration while preserving the bcc Li host, we screen 50 substitutional solutes using density functional theory (DFT) within a funnel based on automatic phase diagram construction, solution energies, solute-vacancy binding energies, and experimental solubility limits. Using an adaptation of the Lomer model for the dilute limit, we show that only Ag, Ge, and Cd solid solutions are predicted to reach $1~\mathrm{mA~cm^{-2}}$ within their solubility limits. The thermodynamically estimated CCD of Ag at $\sim 9$ at.% reaches $\sim 4~\mathrm{mA~cm^{-2}}$ at a theoretical capacity of $1522~\mathrm{mAh~g^{-1}}$. Migration barrier calculations indicate that the enhancement may be partially offset by vacancy trapping, necessitating further validation via molecular dynamics simulations. Notably, Hume-Rothery rules alone prove insufficient as prefilters, whereas machine-learning models trained on the DFT data can eliminate most unsuitable solutes early in the funnel and extend the workflow to related solid-solution searches.

title: A Highly Efficient Depth-Averaged Material Point Method for Geophysical Mass Flows
abstract: Probabilistic hazard assessment of geophysical mass flows requires large simulation ensembles and thus fast and robust numerical models. We present an open-source depth-averaged material point method formulated in global Cartesian coordinates, using Lagrangian particles to track the flow margin. A separate basal friction step based on the Coulomb, Voellmy, or $μ(I)$-rheology brings the flow to rest without artificial stopping criteria. Our model reproduces analytical solutions for a sliding block and dam-break problems and matches the deposit of a laboratory granular column collapse. A back-calculation of the 2023 Brienz/Brinzauls rockslide (Switzerland) at 1m resolution (190'000 particles) runs faster than real time on a single CPU core. Calibrated to the observed runout, the three friction laws yield very similar results, but Coulomb friction shows a slightly wider affected area than Voellmy and $μ(I)$. A probabilistic 1632-simulation ensemble at 5m resolution was computed in 76s. The model is one to two orders of magnitude faster than established depth-averaged models used in engineering practice, making catchment-style ensemble simulations feasible on a desktop computer.

title: Single-molecule cold chemistry: Isotopic branching ratios of the $\mathrm{H_2O^+ + HD}$ reaction at cryogenic temperatures
abstract: Isotopic branching in ion-molecule reactions influences interstellar deuterium fractionation, yet its dynamics remain poorly understood for many important systems at astrophysically relevant temperatures. Here, we investigate H- and D-atom transfer in the $\mathrm{H_2O^+ + HD}$ reaction using single sympathetically cooled water ions in a cryogenic radiofrequency trap. Nondestructive identification of the products from 441 individual reaction events at a mean collision energy of 7 K reveals an $\mathrm{H_3O^+/H_2DO^+}$ product branching ratio of $1.50 \pm 0.15$ demonstrating a preferential H-atom transfer. The experiments are rationalized using quasi-classical-trajectory calculations which indicate a transition from direct dynamics at higher energies to a complex-mediated reaction under the present experimental conditions and point to an important role of intramolecular vibrational redistribution affecting the isotopic branching in this regime. The present results extend measurements into an astrochemically relevant energy regime and establish cryogenic single-ion chemistry as a new platform for resolving competing reaction pathways.

title: Combining Simulations and Spectroscopy to Design Protective Coatings on Sulfide Solid Electrolytes
abstract: Sulfide solid electrolytes are attractive for all-solid-state batteries because of their high Li-ion conductivity and favorable processability, but their practical use is limited by electrochemical instability and moisture-induced degradation. Molecular surface coatings offer a scalable strategy to improve humidity tolerance and interfacial stability, yet there is limited understanding of the molecular-level factors governing surface interactions. By combining large-scale atomistic simulations enabled by a machine-learning potential with targeted experiments, we present a comprehensive framework for designing molecular coatings on Li$_6$PS$_5$Cl (LPSCl). Using a PET-MAD interatomic potential fine-tuned on an r$^2$SCAN reference dataset covering LPSCl surfaces, molecular adsorbates, and their interactions, we model surface adsorption of carboxylic (CA), sulfonic (SA), and phosphonic (PA) acids with alkyl chains of varying lengths and the interaction of these coated surfaces with water at finite temperature. The simulations show that lithiated head groups generally exhibit more favorable adsorption energies. Impedance spectroscopy shows that the lithiated coatings maintain 40--55\% of the initial ionic conductivity after powder processing. While adsorption strength is largely controlled by head-group chemistry and lithiation state, coating morphology depends primarily on alkyl-chain length and surface coverage. In particular, long-chain lithiated carboxylates form dense, brush-like hydrophobic layers that reduce water access to reactive Li surface sites, with protection setting in at a coating thickness of approximately 0.8 nm. Consistent with these predictions, longer carboxylate chains suppress H$_2$S evolution more effectively. Because thicker coatings also hinder Li-ion transport, intermediate chain lengths offer the best balance between moisture protection and ionic conductivity.

title: Rationalizing charge transfer: a single-molecule case study across three distinct surfaces
abstract: Organic molecules are versatile building blocks for the formation of complex low-dimensional nanostructures on surfaces. Recently, interest has grown in translating on-surface synthetic protocols from noble metal surfaces to insulating surfaces, which offer technological relevance, and to magnetic or superconducting surfaces, which offer new routes to correlated phases. It is important, therefore, to understand how these alternative surfaces may alter the properties of adsorbates through processes like charge transfer and screening. Evidence for charge transfer is often obtained experimentally via scanning tunneling microscopy (STM) and spectroscopy (STS), and theoretically via density functional theory (DFT). In this work, we systematically compare the properties of isolated macrocyclic emeraldine (Me$_6$) molecules on three different surfaces: metallic Au(111), a semiconducting ferromagnetic monolayer of FeCl$_2$, and a cleaved superconducting surface of bulk 2H-NbSe$_2$. We show that STS and DFT alone are insufficient to quantify charge transfer for these cases. Instead, we complement these methods with Kelvin probe force microscopy (KPFM) measurements and model Hamiltonian calculations to demonstrate that on Au(111) and FeCl$_2$, Me$_6$ molecules donate a single electron to the substrate, whereas on NbSe$_2$ two electrons are transferred from molecule to substrate. Our work provides insight into the interplay of charge transfer, screening, and molecule-substrate coupling, and develops experimental and theoretical methods for comparing the properties of adsorbates across different surfaces for future studies.

title: CO2-Induced Shifts in the Confined Phase Transformation of CH4 in Metal-Organic Frameworks
abstract: A sharp increase in gas uptake over a narrow pressure range can occur for fluids confined in nanoporous materials such as metal-organic frameworks (MOFs), reflecting a transformation between distinct adsorption states, often accompanied by the existence of metastable states. Understanding how co-adsorbed species modify this behavior is important for predicting and optimizing gas storage and separation. Here, we investigate the effect of CO2 on the adsorption transformation of confined CH4 in rigid IRMOF-1 and IRMOF-8. Transition-Matrix Monte Carlo (TMMC) simulations were performed for systems containing 0-75 and 0-150 CO2 molecules in IRMOF-1 and IRMOF-8, respectively. While the addition of CO2 decreases the maximum CH4 uptake, consistent with competition for pore space, remarkably, the presence of CO2 significantly shifts the discontinuity in the CH4 adsorption isotherm to substantially lower pressures relative to the pure CH4 system. This promotion of the high-density CH4 phase at lower pressures demonstrates that CO2 substantially alters the thermodynamic landscape governing confined CH4 through changes in both fluid-fluid and fluid-framework interactions. These results establish CO2 as a thermodynamic modifier of confined CH4 behavior and suggest that controlled co-adsorption provides a means of tuning adsorption transformations in nanoporous materials.

title: Thermal stabilization of defect charge states and finite-temperature charge transition levels
abstract: Point defects introduce localized electronic states that critically affect carrier trapping, recombination, and transport in functional materials. The associated charge transition level (CTLs) can depend on temperature, requiring accurate treatment of vibrational free energy contributions. In this work, we use machine-learned interatomic potentials to efficiently compute temperature-dependent (CTLs) for vacancies in MgO, LiF, and CsSnBr 3 . Using thermodynamic integration, we quantify free energy differences between charge states and calculate the vibrational entropy contributions at finite temperatures. We find that temperature significantly affects the (CTLs) across all three materials, with substantial energy level shifts in MgO and LiF over the investigated temperature ranges. Most notably, in CsSnBr 3 a neutral charge state becomes thermodynamically stable above 40K, introducing a Fermi-level window absent at 0K. We show that the widely used static, zero-kelvin defect formalism can miss both quantitative (CTL) shifts and the qualitative emergence of new stable charge states.

title: A classical trajectory method for diatom-atom-atom ternary association reactions
abstract: We introduce a classical trajectory method for calculating direct diatom-atom-atom ternary association re- action rates that incorporates the rotational degrees of freedom of the diatomic reactant. By treating the diatomic molecule as a rigid rotor, we include the effects of the anisotropy of the molecule-atom interaction and the dynamical effects of the rotational motion. We apply this approach to a system of experimental interest, CD+ + He + He, along with the isotopic variant CH+ + He + He -> CHHe+ + He, and examine the role of the internal, rotational degrees of freedom of the diatomic molecule. In particular, we find that in the regime where the collision energy is much smaller than the rotational energy of the entrance channel, the rotational motion leads to deviation from the classical threshold law by violating the assumptions of long-range capture theory models.

title: Revisiting 2-Isopropylthioxanthone: Direct and Reactivable Photopolymerization of Acrylates from Near-UV to Blue Light. Efficient 3D Printing and Surface Modification
abstract: Reversible-deactivation radical photopolymerization (photoRDRP) enables precise spatiotemporal control of polymer architectures. Because of embedded active chain ends, photoRDRP offers straightforward reactivation and chain extension, providing unmatched flexibility for fine-tuning structural, mechanical, and physicochemical properties for targeted applications.

title: Thermal convective and flow dynamics of blood trihybrid nanofluid inside a stenosis artery for cardiovascular disease treatment using artificial intelligence approach
abstract: This article briefly discusses the influence of heat radiation and heat source on the convective flow of a blood-based trihybrid nanofluid inside a stenotic artery with chemical reaction. It can assist in investigating and predicting blood flow dynamics and heat transmission in constricted arteries for thermal therapy, targeted drug delivery, and cardiovascular disease treatment. By replicating the intricate interactions of many nanoparticles with blood, the model also aids in the design and optimization of biomedical devices like stents and artificial organs. The AI technique also makes it possible to make quick, precise, and patient-specific predictions, which helps doctors plan treatments and enhances the efficacy of cardiovascular procedures. The artificial intelligent neural network (AINN) is one sophisticated machine learning approach. The difficulty led to the system of PDEs (partial differential equations), which are transformed into ODEs (ordinary differential equations) via dimensionless similarity. The dataset was filtered using the Bvp4c method before being incorporated into the Bayesian-regularization algorithm (BRA). Regression-based statistical analysis, error histograms, absolute error, and MSE (mean squared error) are used to measure the determination, verification, convergence, and stability of Bayesian-regularized neural network mappings for this hybrid model. title: Artificial intelligence in rational drug discovery: optimization of lead compounds and in-silico prediction of molecular interactions for faster pharmaceutical development
abstract: The conventional drug discovery process is intricate, expensive and time-consuming with high attrition rates. Addressing these inefficiencies has spelled the dawn of artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) as game-changers in rational drug design. The review highlights the revolutionary potential of AI techniques such as deep learning and generative models in drug discovery and development. We discuss how AI improves protein-ligand interaction predictions and quantitative structure-activity relationship (QSAR) modelling, as well as virtual screening, in drug discovery.

title: Specification of Origins of DNA Replication Within Distinct Chromatin States in Human Cells
abstract: A comprehensive map of binding sites for the Origin Recognition Complex (ORC) in the human genome reveals relationships among replication licensing, chromatin state, three-dimensional genome organization, location of origins of DNA replication and DNA replication timing. Defining these relationships is essential for understanding how replication licensing is integrated with the broader organization and duplication of the human genome. Using 30 high-quality ORC1 CUT&RUN datasets, an ORC1 three-dimensional binding matrix (ORC1 3DM) was constructed that captures genomic position, binding intensity, and reproducibility across replicates. This analysis reveals considerable heterogeneity in ORC1 binding, and integration with chromatin-state maps shows that ORC1-binding sites separate into distinct epigenomic groups, with high-confidence sites enriched in H2A{middle dot}Z1- and H3K4me3- associated open chromatin. Hi-C analysis demonstrates preferential localization of ORC1 binding to sub-regions of genomic A compartments and frequent association with loop anchors, supported by a direct interaction between ORC1 and CTCF. Replication-timing analysis shows that ORC1 binding sites are enriched in initiation zones and exhibit subgroup-specific temporal patterns. An integrated analysis combining multiple replication initiation assays and chromatin features further places ORC1 3DM within a unified replication-chromatin framework. Together, these results support a hierarchical, probabilistic model of replication licensing that is embedded within chromatin architecture.

title: CochleaNet: deep learning-based image analysis for cochlear connectomics and gene therapy
abstract: With the emergence of gene and optogenetic therapies targeting deafness, the comprehensive analysis of the molecular anatomy and physiology of the cochlea has become ever more important. Here, we introduce CochleaNet, a deep learning-based framework to analyze volumetric imaging data obtained by light-sheet microscopy of decalcified, cleared and fluorescently labeled cochleae.
venue: Molecular therapy : the journal of the American Society of Gene Therapy

title: Modified NSAIDs as potential inhibitors of phosphopeptide recognition by the BRCA1 tandem BRCT domain
abstract: Small molecules that disrupt phosphopeptide recognition by the tandem BRCT (tBRCT) domain of BRCA1 are of interest as a means of suppressing homologous recombination (HR) repair and of sensitising tumor cells to poly (ADP-ribose) polymerase inhibitors (PARPi). Here we report an entirely computational design and prioritisation study of amide derivatives assembled from non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID) fragments and intended to occupy the pSer-X-X-Phe recognition cleft of BRCA1 tBRCT.

title: From Healthcare Data to Actionable Intelligence: An Integrative Review and Gated Framework for Trustworthy Al-Enabled Healthcare Analytics
abstract: Background: The increasing availability of electronic health records, clinical narratives, biomedical literature, imaging, physiological signals, and patient-generated data has created substantial opportunities for artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled healthcare analytics. Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) and large language models (LLMs) can extract, summarize, synthesize, and transform heterogeneous healthcare information. However, AI-generated information does not automatically constitute reliable or actionable intelligence.

title: Structure and antigenicity of the 2026 Bundibugyo virus glycoprotein
abstract: An outbreak of ebolavirus disease caused by a new zoonotic spillover of Bundibugyo virus (BDBV) is currently spreading at an unprecedented pace in the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Uganda. The outbreak has resulted in 7,733 cases with a case-fatality ratio of 48%, yet no BDBV-specific vaccines or therapeutics are available. The ebolavirus glycoprotein (GP) promotes viral entry and is the target of neutralizing antibodies and vaccine development. Here, we engineered a soluble, prefusion-stabilized GP trimer from a contemporary BDBV isolate and determined its cryo-electron microscopy structure bound to the broadly neutralizing antibody EBOV-515. It reveals the molecular basis for EBOV-515 cross-reactivity and suggests that the antibody inhibits viral entry by interfering with NPC1 engagement in addition to trapping GP in the prefusion conformation and hindering glycan cap cleavage. Mapping lineage-defining substitutions identified changes in GP1 and GP2, including R506S within an antigenic site targeted by multiple broadly neutralizing antibodies recognizing the fusion loop. Nevertheless, we found that several glycan cap-, GP base-, and HR2-directed antibodies cross-reacted and neutralized BDBV DRC/2026 GP pseudovirus with potency comparable or greater to that observed against earlier BDBV isolates and the Zaire ebolavirus Makona/2024 isolate. These findings define the antigenic properties of contemporary BDBV GP and delineate conserved epitopes as ideal targets for antibody therapeutics and for the development of pan-ebolavirus vaccines.

title: High Defect Formation Energies Limit Ionic Conductivity in Na3Ga2Li3F12 and Na3Al2Li3F12
abstract: Lithium-conducting fluoride garnets exhibit ionic conductivities of ∼10–10 S cm–1, far below those of their oxide counterparts. Here, we investigate the origin of this poor transport in Na3Ga2Li3F12 and Na3Al2Li3F12 through a combination of structural characterization and first-principles calculations. Both compounds are highly ordered, with no significant antisite disorder, and exhibit intrinsic ionic conductivities of ∼2 × 10–11 S cm–1 at 100 °C. Nudged elastic band calculations reveal low Li-ion migration barriers (0.16 to 0.29 eV), indicating that the fluoride garnet framework does not inherently restrict Li-ion diffusion. However, the formation energies for lithium Frenkel and Schottky defect pairs are high (1.9 to 2.4 eV), indicating that the intrinsic concentrations of mobile Li-ion defects are negligibly small. These results establish that the low conductivity of stoichiometric fluoride garnets arises from high defect-formation energies, rather than high migration barriers.

title: From Atoms to Reactors: A Critical Review of a Decade of Machine Learning in Heterogeneous Catalysis (2017-2026).
abstract: This critical review traces the evolution of machine learning (ML) across the full value chain of heterogeneous catalysis over 2017-2026, from catalyst discovery to reactor and process design, and across the principal reaction families (CO2 reduction, water splitting, nitrogen chemistry, zeolite-catalyzed transformations). Each stage is evaluated against four criteria - data foundation, method maturity, experimental validation and deployment readiness - through a structured capability scorecard.

title: Metabolic engineering of Yarrowia lipolytica for higher fatty alcohol production
abstract: Fatty alcohols are versatile chemicals with growing demand across a broad range of industries, yet conventional production methods pose environmental challenges. Microbial biosynthesis offers a promising alternative, if hosts can be engineered to achieve high product titers. The industrially relevant oleaginous yeast Yarrowia lipolytica is well suited to this challenge because of its natural capacity for lipid metabolism. Here, we engineered Y. lipolytica W29 for fatty alcohol production by disrupting pathways involved in lipogenesis and fatty alcohol oxidation, identifying fatty alcohol oxidation as a major constraint on product accumulation. Initial engineering yielded fatty alcohol titers of 2.5 g/L from 40 g/L glucose. Subsequent optimization of media supplements and nutrient concentrations, combined with deletion of the citrate transporter CEX1 and addition of 1% Tergitol to the extractive culture medium, increased titers to 10.9 g/L in shake flasks with 80 g/L glucose and a carbon-to-nitrogen ratio of 60. Scaling the process to fed-batch bioreactor cultivation further increased titers to 19.4 g/L. These results demonstrate that combining metabolic engineering with medium and process optimization enables high-titer fatty alcohol production in Y. lipolytica.

title: Conformational Reorganization of a Processive Cellulase on Crystalline Cellulose
abstract: Enzymes that degrade insoluble polymers must couple catalytic chemistry to productive engagement with heterogeneous substrate interfaces, yet direct structural information on these interfacial states remains limited. We investigated the conformational organization of the processive cellulase Trichoderma reesei Cel7A both free in solution and bound to an insoluble cellulose substrate using small-angle neutron scattering (SANS). Use of biosynthetically deuterated bacterial cellulose allowed the scattering contribution of the cellulose-associated Cel7A holoenzyme to be selectively highlighted using SANS with contrast matching. SANS measurements performed under conditions supporting high or low catalytic activity revealed distinct differences between the free and cellulose-bound enzyme. Under poorly active conditions, the conformational distributions of free and bound Cel7A were similar. In contrast, catalytically favorable conditions produced an additional interdomain correlation in the bound enzyme, consistent with redistribution toward a substrate-selected conformational ensemble. Molecular dynamics simulations showed that free Cel7A samples can assume compact, intermediate, and extended conformations, but these solution-state ensembles did not reproduce the structural features of cellulose-bound Cel7A. These results identify productive cellulose engagement as a structurally distinct state of the Cel7A holoenzyme and support a dynamic model in which the linker and carbohydrate-binding module modulate interfacial positioning of the catalytic domain rather than functioning as a rigid mechanical unit during processive hydrolysis. More broadly, the findings suggest that heterogeneous biocatalysis depends not only on substrate binding and active-site chemistry, but also on interface-selected conformational states that determine whether binding becomes productive. The study further demonstrates how deuteration and neutron contrast variation can reveal functional macromolecular conformations directly within complex interfacial environments.

title: Potatoes could be the secret to better plant-based meat, say food scientists
abstract: Potatoes could hold the key to making better gluten-free plant-based meat, according to a new study.

title: Unraveling Water Balances behind Salt Formation in CO2 Reduction Electrolyzers
abstract: Salt precipitation in CO2 electrolyzers remains a critical barrier to long-term stability, yet the underlying water-salt transport and balance are poorly understood. Here, we established a quantitative mass balance framework to account for water entering and leaving the cathode chamber from all possible sources and across different phases, thereby elucidating the origin of bicarbonate salt formation.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: A tiny defect in a crystal reveals a big quantum surprise
abstract: Researchers have solved a long-standing challenge in understanding how tiny defects in materials like diamond and silicon carbide behave when exposed to light. Their new computational method revealed a surprisingly important energy-loss mechanism in silicon carbide that scientists had previously underestimated. The finding helps explain a mystery that has puzzled researchers for years and could improve the design of quantum computers and sensors.

title: AI-Driven Discovery Pipeline Identifies Carvedilol as a Novel Partial Agonist of THRβ
abstract: Thyroid hormone receptor beta (THRβ) is a key therapeutic target for metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease and dyslipidemia, yet the discovery of structurally diverse agonists remains challenging. Here, we developed an AI-driven hierarchical drug discovery framework integrating graph neural network (GNN)-based virtual screening, structure-based modeling, and multilevel biological validation to accelerate THRβ agonist identification.
venue: Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling

title: New test measures potentially harmful metals in cellulose food packaging
abstract: A technique for detecting potentially harmful metals in regenerated cellulose food packaging is discussed in the International Journal of Environment and Pollution. The new tool can be used for safety assessments of materials increasingly used as alternatives to conventional plastics.

title: Interfacial topological selection links structural motifs to the free-energy barrier in methane hydrate nucleation
abstract: HypothesisMethane hydrate nucleation is a stochastic process critical to energy and flow-assurance technologies, yet the structural changes associated with crossing its free-energy barrier remain poorly resolved. We hypothesize that transient topological motifs in the interface hydrogen-bonded network provide information about barrier crossing beyond bulk nucleus growth alone.SimulationsTo test this hypothesis, we integrate molecular dynamics (MD) simulations with machine learning (ML).
venue: Journal of colloid and interface science

title: Radical–Electrochemical Coupling Enables Amination of Methane
abstract: The selective functionalization of methane under ambient conditions is widely regarded as a holy grail in chemistry, yet remains fundamentally limited not only by the inertness of the C–H bond but also by the transient nature of highly reactive intermediates. Short-lived species are often difficult to preserve and utilize prior to productive coupling, constraining accessible reaction pathways and product selectivity.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Lightweight open-source reasoning large language model for evidence synthesis screening
abstract: ObjectivesTo evaluate performance and efficiency of a lightweight open-source reasoning large language model (LLM) against an expert-derived reference standard for screening scientific publication databases.Materials and methodsTwo expert reviewers screened subsets of database records across 3 stages: (1) base eligibility (n = 200), (2) obesity focus (n = 200), and (3) women of reproductive age focus (n = 150). The LLM (gpt-oss-20b) screened all records (n = 20 118). Performance (F1-score and sensitivity [recall]) and efficiency (average screening rate) were assessed.ResultsInterreader agreement was near-perfect ( κ : 0.99-1.00; all P .001). LLM performance was high: F1-score, 0.83-0.94; sensitivity, 90%-95%; specificity, 86%-99%; accuracy, 89%-94%; precision, 77%-99%; and negative predictive value (NPV), 89%-96%. LLM screening was faster than reviewers (19.4 vs ∼1.0 records/min).DiscussionThe LLM achieved high performance and efficiency relative to an expert-derived reference standard for screening.ConclusionThe use of lightweight open-source reasoning LLMs shows promise to support screening in evidence synthesis workflows.

title: Chronic fentanyl induces sex-specific anxiolytic-like effects in opioid-dependent rats
abstract: Fentanyl is used as a treatment for severe pain, and it is a major contributor to opioid misuse and overdose fatalities. While it has been established that opioids are widely misused for their euphoric effects, little is known about the effects of chronic fentanyl exposure on anxiety-like behavior. We determined the effects of chronic fentanyl on anxiety-like behavior, locomotor activity, dependence, and body weight in adult male and female Wistar rats (n = 8 per sex and treatment) that received saline or fentanyl (0.6 mg/kg/day) via minipumps. Locomotor activity was measured in a small open field (SOF) before pump implantation. After implantation, rats were retested in the SOF, evaluated for anxiety-like behavior in the elevated plus-maze (EPM) and large open field (LOF), and it was determined if they were opioid dependent by counting somatic withdrawal signs. Fentanyl increased locomotor activity in the SOF and the LOF. In the EPM, fentanyl increased open-arm time in males but not in females. In the LOF, fentanyl increased entries into, and shortened the latency to enter, the anxiogenic inner zones, most prominently in females. Naloxone precipitated a somatic withdrawal syndrome in fentanyl-treated rats of both sexes, and fentanyl prevented body weight gain in males and attenuated it in females. To provide insight into the behavior across the LOF and EPM, an additional correlational analysis was conducted. In saline-treated males, but not females, anxiety-related measures were correlated between the two tests. Rats that made more open-arm entries in the EPM made more entries into, and spent more time in, the center zone of the LOF (r = 0.78 and 0.75), and the percentage of time on the open arms correlated with time spent in the middle zone of the LOF (r = 0.73). In conclusion, fentanyl decreases anxiety-like behavior in opioid dependent animals. These findings have significant implications as they suggest that dependent individuals might continue to misuse fentanyl for its anxiolytic effects. Furthermore, patients treated with chronic fentanyl for severe pain and comorbid anxiety might continue to benefit from the drug's anxiolytic effects.

title: Cooperative Dual-Template Assembly of Bimodal Interconnected Mesoporous Carbon Nanospheres with Boosted Charge Transport
abstract: Mesoporous materials have attracted great research attention since their first advent in 1990s; however, the self-assembly of soft micelles can generate only unary periodicity. A feasible strategy capable of building multinary pore structures remains scarcely explored due to huge synthetic difficulty. Herein, we explore a cooperative dual-template assembly route, which allows for compatible interaction of Pluronic P123 and L64 in solution, to successfully construct a type of mesoporous carbon nanospheres with bimodal mesopores. The key to such construction of hierarchical mesopores from a pure soft-template process without recruitment of a hard template mainly relies on the formation of composite micelles with both suitable mutual interactions and individually stabilized condensed states. The resultant mesoporous carbon spheres possess good uniformity in morphology and mesoporosity, including a mean particle size at ∼200 nm, a high surface area of 537 m2 g–1, and an interconnected bimodal mesopore size centered at 11.1 and 4.2 nm along with a massive amount of micropores. Moreover, this dual-template assembly strategy allows for precise structural regulation over the pore curvature and pore size through tailoring the reaction conditions. As a proof of concept, the fabricated bimodal mesoporous carbon, as an ammonium-ion battery anode, showcases excellent electrochemical performances owing to its permeable and gradient porous structure for fast mass and charge transfer. Our study underscores a facile and extendable toolbox for synthesizing complex or hierarchical mesostructures as advanced energy model materials.

title: Breaking Symmetry Cancellation: Heterovalent Substitution Unlocks Ultrastrong, Phase-Matchable Nonlinearity in Deep-Ultraviolet Tetrahedral Crystals
abstract: Deep-ultraviolet (deep-UV) nonlinear optical (NLO) crystals demand a challenging integration of strong second-harmonic generation (SHG), sufficient birefringence for phase matching (PM), and a wide bandgap (λ < 200 nm). In tetrahedron-based materials, the hyperpolarizabilities of constituent tetrahedra usually nearly cancel due to structural symmetry, resulting in weak SHG and small birefringence─a classic example being α-SiO2. Breaking this symmetry-driven cancellation while retaining deep-UV transparency thus represents a key chemical design challenge.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Solid–Liquid Transitions in 1D Metal–Organic Chalcogenolates
abstract: A lack of melt processability is noted for emerging hybrid material systems like metal–organic frameworks, lead-halide perovskites, and metal–organic chalcogenolates (MOChas). Here, we report reversible solid-to-liquid phase transitions ranging from 67 to 184 °C in silver secondary-alkanethiolate 1-dimensional (1D) MOChas. These MOChas were synthesized using five different secondary alkanethiols: 2-propanethiol, 2-butanethiol, 2-pentanethiol, 3-hexanethiol, and 4-heptanethiol.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society
